passage: At the Rotterdam warehouse, Lucia was closing the last delivery when Mateo pulled her by the shelves. "I skipped the crane check this morning, no time. I signed the sheet anyway. Keep it quiet, yes? You'd do it for me." She liked Mateo. He had covered her shift when her mother was ill. Her stomach tightened. "Mateo, I can't lie for you. If someone asks me, I'll tell the truth." He blinked. "So what do I do?" "Do the check now, before the afternoon shift, and tell the supervisor it was late. I'll stay with you while you do it." They walked to the crane together in silence. Lucia was not sure Mateo forgave her, but she felt lighter than if she had joined the silence.

qa.q: Why did Lucia's stomach tighten when Mateo asked her to keep quiet?
qa.a: Lucia felt torn: she liked Mateo and owed him for covering her shift, but she could not lie for him.

qa.q: What could Lucia do if Mateo refuses to tell the supervisor?
qa.a: She can remind Mateo she will not lie if asked, encourage him again, and report it to the supervisor herself if the risk continues.

qa.q: How might Mateo have felt when Lucia refused?
qa.a: He blinked and asked what to do, so he was probably surprised and worried. He may also have felt let down by a friend, since Lucia was not sure he forgave her.

grounding: A friendly colleague asks the protagonist to keep quiet about his shortcut; she urges him to fix it and says she cannot lie for him.

passage:
'Preeti, you didn't see anything, okay?' Yogesh said, closing the quality sheet.
'I saw you tick all twelve checks on a batch you tested for two minutes.'
'The line was behind. Mehta-sir wanted the pallets out by six. It's fine, the last ten batches were fine.'
'And if this one isn't?'
'It will be. Come on. We've been lunch partners for a year. You're not going to report me.'
Preeti's stomach knotted. He had covered her shifts twice when her mother was ill.
'I'm not running to anyone. But I'm not lying for you either. If someone asks me, I'll tell the truth.'
'So you'll report me.'
'I'm telling you to fix it first. Test the batch properly now. It's twenty minutes. I'll help you pull the samples.'
Yogesh stared at the sheet for a long moment. Then he tore it off the clipboard. 'Twenty minutes.'
'I'll get the gloves.'

qa.q: How many checks did Yogesh tick?
What was Preeti feeling when Yogesh mentioned their year as lunch partners?
qa.a: Preeti felt torn and uneasy, her stomach knotting, because loyalty to Yogesh clashed with honesty.
She urged him to fix it first, offered to help, and was clear she would not lie if asked.

qa.q: How does Yogesh see Preeti's refusal to stay quiet?
qa.a: Yogesh first takes it as betrayal, then accepts it and retests the batch.

grounding: Shows a friendly colleague asking Preeti to stay quiet about his shortcut, and her urging him to fix it while refusing to lie for him.

passage: My name is Jomon, and I learned this one the slow way. At the hotel in Kochi where I trained as a junior chef, Arnab ran the cold room. He was the friendliest person in the kitchen, the one who saved you a plate at 2 a.m. In my second month I noticed he was writing fridge temperatures in the log without checking the thermometer. 'It's always fine,' he said. 'Don't make it a thing.' So I didn't. For three weeks I said nothing. Then the chef asked me to countersign the log. That was the moment it stopped being Arnab's shortcut and became my signature on something I knew was false. I went to Arnab first. 'Check it properly from today, and mark the missing readings honestly, or I can't sign.' He was angry for a day. Then he started checking. I still like him. I just don't sign what I haven't seen.

qa.q: What did the chef ask Jomon to do?
qa.a: The chef asked Jomon to countersign the log.

qa.q: What was Jomon likely feeling when asked to countersign?
qa.a: Jomon felt uneasy and caught, realising the silence had turned into signing something false.

qa.q: What did Jomon say to Arnab, and why was it wise?
qa.a: To check properly and mark the missing readings honestly or Jomon couldn't sign, which gave Arnab a chance to fix it without Jomon lying.

qa.q: How might Arnab have felt when Jomon refused to sign?
qa.a: Arnab was angry for a day, perhaps feeling let down by a friend, before starting to check properly.

grounding: A first-person account of joining a friendly colleague's silence about a shortcut until it became Jomon's problem, then asking him to fix it and refusing to cover.
